classification.difficultyReason: Choose between parallel-line and same-vertex relationships in a mixed collection and give brief reasons.

content.prompt: For each diagram, calculate the value of the missing angles. Give a brief reason.

spec.description: Horizontal transversal across two parallel lines rising right; single upper-right parallel arrows, six plain endpoints, no angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: 130° and a° occupy corresponding lower-right sectors.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 130° and unknown a° are visible.

answer.worked:
Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal.
$$a=130^\circ$$

spec.description: Two shallow parallel lines rise right, crossed by a steep rising transversal; right-pointing single parallel marks and six plain endpoints.
spec.mathematics: a° at the upper intersection and 70° at the lower intersection occupy corresponding lower-left sectors.
spec.answerVisibility: Only a° and the given 70° are visible.

answer.worked:
Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal.
$$a=70^\circ$$

spec.description: Horizontal transversal crosses two steep parallel lines descending right; upper-arm arrows point upper-left.
spec.mathematics: 110° lies above the transversal inside the pair at the left vertex; a° lies below it inside the pair at the right vertex. Alternate interior angles.

answer.worked:
Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.
$$a=110^\circ$$

spec.description: Two steep descending parallel lines, upper-left parallel arrows, and a shallow descending transversal; six plain endpoints.
spec.mathematics: a° above the transversal at the left vertex and 120° below it at the right vertex are alternate interior angles.

answer.worked:
Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.
$$a=120^\circ$$

spec.description: Two shallow descending parallel lines with lower-right arrows; nearly vertical transversal leans right downwards. Retain the unlabelled lower intersection.
spec.mathematics: a° in the upper-right sector and 130° in the lower-left sector share the upper vertex and are vertically opposite.

spec.description: Two shallow rising parallel lines with right-pointing marks and a steep rising transversal. Preserve the lower unlabelled parallel line.
spec.mathematics: 67° in the upper-right sector and a° in the lower-left sector are vertically opposite at the upper intersection.

spec.description: Two diagonal rising parallel lines, upper-right arrows on their lower-left arms, crossed by a steep descending transversal.
spec.mathematics: 115° at the upper intersection and a° at the lower intersection are interior angles on the right side of the transversal.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles between parallel lines sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}115^\circ+a&=180^\circ\\a&=65^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two horizontal parallel lines, single right-pointing marks, and a descending transversal.
spec.mathematics: a° below the upper parallel and 62° above the lower parallel are co-interior on the left of the transversal.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles between parallel lines sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}62^\circ+a&=180^\circ\\a&=118^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two shallow descending parallel lines with lower-right marks and a nearly vertical transversal rising slightly right.
spec.mathematics: a° at the upper intersection and 100° at the lower intersection occupy corresponding upper-right sectors.

answer.worked:
Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal.
$$a=100^\circ$$

spec.description: Two near-vertical parallel lines with upward single marks and a rising transversal. Apply the explicit editorial decision: locate a° with an arc at the left vertex, opposite 117°. The right intersection is unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: 117° and a° share the left vertex and occupy vertically opposite obtuse sectors.
spec.answerVisibility: 117° is given; a° and its identifying arc are question content. The result is answer-only.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles at the left intersection are equal.
$$a=117^\circ$$

spec.description: Two shallow rising parallel lines with upper-right marks, crossed by a steep rising transversal.
spec.mathematics: 64° below the upper parallel and a° above the lower parallel are co-interior to the left of the transversal.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles between parallel lines sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}64^\circ+a&=180^\circ\\a&=116^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two diagonal descending parallel lines with upper-left marks on their lower-right arms, crossed by a shallow rising transversal.
spec.mathematics: 116° above the transversal at the left intersection and a° below it at the right intersection are alternate interior angles.

answer.worked:
Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.
$$a=116^\circ$$
